source.section: Schedule 1 line 26 (PDF page 17: born January 1, 1953 through January 1, 1959 and 'reached the age of 67 on or before December 31, 2025 ... You are considered to turn 67 the day before your 67th birthday'); Worksheet 2 lines 1-11 (PDF page 18); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = interest 15,000.00 = 15,000.00. Federal taxable income = 15,000.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 0.00 (floored at 0); given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan: born January 1, 1959, the last birth date in the Tier 3 range. The 67th birthday is January 1, 2026, but the booklet treats a person as turning 67 the day before the birthday, December 31, 2025, so the age test is met for 2025 although the age at year end by the calendar is 66. Worksheet 2 line 1 20,000.00; line 7 20,000.00; line 8 0.00; line 9 exemption 5,800.00; line 11 Tier 3 = 14,200.00 (the projection, without line 9, has 20,000.00). By the form: line 14 = 15,000.00 - 14,200.00 = 800.00; exemption 5,800.00; line 16 = 0.00 (with the projection's 20,000.00, line 14 is 0.00 and line 16 0.00). Tax 0.00; state income tax 0.00. Without Tier 3 (age taken as 66): taxable 9,200.00, tax 391.00. Age input 67 by the tax rule (a person reaches an age the day before the birthday; brief 5b).
